title: Praise of the Hearth & Tungtap (Kor I Tungtap)
cultural_context: Humorous and affectionate traditional domestic phawar celebrating fermented fish chutney (Tungtap) eaten around the clay hearth.
lyrics_khasi:
Haba sngi ka la sep
Bad u slap u la hap,
Ngi shong sawdong rympei
Ban bam ja bad tungtap;
Iiwbih thiang ba bang,
U sohmynken u sat,
Ka ja sotti ba syaid
Ka pynkmen ia ka kpoh.

Wat la ngi don ha ri thor,
Ne ha kyllood ki shnong,
Ka sur jong i tungtap
Ka ring ia ka mynsiem;
Ngi kynmaw la ka tnum,
Ka dpei jong ka mei-rad,
Hangta ka jingsuk
Ba u Blei u la theh.
lyrics_english:
When the sun has set
And the rain pours down,
We sit encircling the hearth
To eat warm rice and tungtap;
Savory pungent aroma,
Fiery wild chilies,
Steaming indigenous hill-rice
Bringing joy to the belly.

Though we may travel to distant plains,
Or roam faraway towns,
The taste of humble tungtap
Draws back the longing heart;
We remember our thatched roof,
The hearth of our grandmother,
Where true peace resides
Poured down by God above.
